newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to raise public transport subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to raise public transport subsidies.

text.p: The government agreed Monday to increase subsidies for public transport to prevent a rise in gasoline prices from leading to higher bus fares.
Transport and Communications Minister Moises Orozco Graterol told reporters the subsidy for public transport operators would be raised 27.3 percent.
The government plans to raise domestic gasoline price to an average of 70 bolivars ($0.14) per liter July 31.

"The gasoline price is increasing 27.3 percent and the subsidy will rise by the same proportion. That means, in theory, that fares should not go up," said Eduardo Blanco, coordinator of commerce and supply at state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela.

Public transport fares in Venezuela are a sensitive political issue and traditionally have been heavily subsidized. For each vehicle of 32 seats or more, bus operators currently receive a monthly subsidy of 108,000 bolivars ($220) per month to pay for fuel and another 20,000 bolivars ($40) to compensate for cheaper student fares.
Full bus fares within Caracas average between 50 and 70 bolivars ($0.10 to $0.14). The decision to increase transport subsidies must be approved by the full cabinet Wednesday.
